blocking_focus: AK-74M short mouse/gamepad presses still over-commit ammunition.
Enemy hits retain shot identity and damage response but lack readable muzzle, tracer or impact presentation in the captured hit frames.
Ordinary gameplay cannot progress beyond the spawn-to-Alpha route; mouse and gamepad look probes leave yaw unchanged and terminal paths remain unreachable.
Persisted 200% UI scale and motion settings remain disconnected from runtime owners, and Escape is multiply bound.
Three consecutive checkpoint restores leave stale damage and input receipts; measured software-rendered runtime was approximately 7 FPS.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `clean_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Deliver a coherent, accessible title-to-deployment shell and an atomic checkpoint-restore boundary, while preserving the accepted title/HUD/map/weapon/enemy systems and enabling authoritative UI, restart, and hardware-performance verification.

diagnosis.root_cause: The product shell exposes the required pages and persisted settings, but ownership is fragmented: runtime application handles only volume/FOV, subtitle sizing is separately patched by ProductShell, UI scale and motion controls have no shared runtime binding, and Escape is dispatched through overlapping shell/player actions. The briefing is still a static four-paragraph page rather than a timed full-viewport presentation. Separately, checkpoint restoration restores authoritative health, ammo, and 18 stable enemies but does not define a complete transient-state boundary: player damage receipts survive, weapon restoration intentionally copies pre-restore shot/impact histories, and input receipts are not cleared or epoch-scoped. The reported frame rate was collected under Mesa llvmpipe, so it cannot support a candidate performance diagnosis.

stop_conditions: Stop and repair before handoff if clean_boot, resource loading, or script parsing regresses.
Do not accept the shell if one Escape/back press causes multiple transitions, merely releases the gameplay mouse, or produces no context-appropriate transition.
Do not accept 200% UI scale if any critical title, briefing, HUD, pause, settings, or result field clips, leaves the 5% safe area, or obscures combat-critical content.
Do not accept the briefing if it remains a persistent prose dump, can commit deployment more than once, or media failure produces a black or unresponsive page.

Stop restart validation if authoritative checkpoint truth changes incorrectly, enemy identities duplicate/change, a restore transaction remains partially committed, or pre-restore damage/input/shot presentation is exposed as current state.

Do not claim the performance requirement passed from llvmpipe or another software renderer; require a 1920×1080 hardware-capable capture, including the explosion window, and leave performance unqualified if that environment or reachable window is unavailable.

strategy.rationale: First consolidate page input and accessibility under explicit runtime owners while replacing the rejected briefing surface. Then repair restart drift at the transaction boundary by separating authoritative checkpoint data from transient receipts and presentation caches. This directly addresses both required gaps without reopening preserved assets or pulling deferred combat/finale work into the iteration.

code: Run the frozen clean_boot validation and require zero script/resource-load errors.
Statically verify that Escape is not mapped to competing context actions and that shell input handlers consume exactly one routed transition.
Exercise settings save/load/application with assertions for UI scale, subtitle size, FOV, reduced motion, and screen shake runtime-owner state.
Run deterministic damage/fire/restore integration checks for three cycles, including failure-path cleanup and monotonic or epoch-qualified event IDs.
runtime: GameLoop Runtime/Tester must probe title → loadout → loading → briefing → deployment, then pause → settings → resume, checking application state and exactly one transition for each Escape/controller-back press.
Restart the process with UI scale 200% and motion settings persisted; compare shell, HUD, player, and terminal runtime state with the stored values.
Capture the briefing at opening, timed-caption progression, skip/completion, and fallback; verify deployment_commit_count advances once only.

For three separate stepped windows, accumulate player damage and weapon input/shot receipts, restore the checkpoint, and require snapshot health/ammo, 18 stable enemy identities, a completed new restore epoch, and no stale current receipts or feedback effects; inspect clean runtime logs after each cycle independently rather than relying on a final aggregate state alone. Preserve the mission audit.
visual: At 1280×720 and 200% UI scale, capture title, briefing, gameplay HUD, pause/settings, and result surfaces; verify 5% safe-area containment, typography, focus, legibility, and no reticle/viewmodel/route obstruction.

Compare briefing opening and mid-sequence frames: require full-viewport grounded industrial imagery, no persistent four-paragraph prose block, at most two timed caption lines, no baked text/branding, and no black fallback.
Capture gameplay immediately after checkpoint restore and verify that damage arcs, pain tint, hit/impact residues, old combat notices, and stale weapon-result presentation are absent.

On a hardware-capable renderer at 1920×1080, capture bounded frame-time series for representative normal combat and the explosion peak; require approximately 16.7 ms normal frame time and no three consecutive explosion frames below 45 FPS. If ordinary progression cannot reach the explosion window, report that evidence limitation and do not pass the performance criterion.

done_when: A full-viewport industrial briefing presentation uses timed native captions with no more than two active lines, supports completion/skip and a matched non-black fallback, and permits exactly one authoritative deployment transition.

Persisted UI scale, subtitle treatment, FOV, reduced-camera-motion, and screen-shake values are applied after runtime owners exist and remain effective across title, gameplay, pause, terminal presentation, result, and process restart.
At 1280×720 with UI scale set to 200%, all critical fields remain within the 5% safe area, readable, and free of clipping or overlap with the reticle, objectives, enemies, and viewmodel.
Each Escape or controller-back press has one context owner: back navigation on loadout/briefing/settings, pause/resume during gameplay, and no competing player mouse-release transition.
The preserved full-viewport title background, Barlow Condensed typography, authored focus treatment, title/loadout navigation, runtime vitals, minimap, and weapon-ammo HUD remain intact.
tasks.instructions: Unify shell navigation, input consumption, and accessibility application around explicit runtime owners. Remove the overlapping Escape dispatch across pause, menu-back/ui-cancel, and PrototypePlayer; route one physical press through the active application context and consume it once. Replace the prose-only briefing with a full-viewport, state-driven cinematic/caption sequence whose completion or skip exposes deployment without owning mission truth. Apply persisted settings through stable bindings to the responsive shell/HUD roots and to the player/terminal motion owners; reduced motion and screen shake must remain independent. Preserve the accepted title, font, focus, loadout, HUD components, and authored map. If visible briefing media is created or rebound, use this asset-family plan: family_id=briefing_background; prd_style_match=grounded late-morning military-base/industrial tension with no commercial branding; source_quality_class=product-owned or license-verified native video/still suitable for full-viewport use; material_and_texture_evidence=inspect decoded runtime frames for sharp opaque coverage, coherent grading, no matte/edge contamination, no baked text/logos, and verify the actual scene binding; expected_runtime_uses_or_visible_area_share=one justified semantic singleton covering the briefing viewport; minimum_distinct_source_variants=1; minimum_runtime_variants=1; maximum_single_variant_share=1.0; diversity_axes=timed visual progression, caption timing, completion/skip/fallback states; background_mode=opaque full-bleed media with a matched still fallback; runtime_evidence_views=briefing opening, mid-caption, completion/skip boundary, fallback, and 200%-scale layout.

done_when: After damage and weapon fire, three consecutive checkpoint restores each recover the snapshot health, weapon/ammunition state, objective state, countdown rule, and exactly 18 stable enemy identities without duplication.

After every restore, player last-damage/current damage-commit state, weapon input receipts, shot/impact presentation histories, live impacts, damage overlays, and other transient caches are empty or explicitly scoped to the new restore epoch; pre-restore values are never reported as current.

Authoritative event uniqueness remains safe through monotonic serials or epoch-qualified IDs, while the current restore receipt reports the checkpoint version, restore epoch, restored actor count, and transient-reset completion.
A failed substep cannot leave checkpoint_restore_in_progress true or partially resume combat; the transaction either commits coherently or reports failure while remaining quiescent.
No candidate performance conclusion is inferred from the prior software-rendered sample; the candidate remains instrumentable for host-owned 1920×1080 normal-combat and explosion-window profiling.
tasks.instructions: Make checkpoint restoration an explicit atomic boundary. Keep the working snapshot restoration and enemy-roster epoch transaction, but add coordinated player, weapon, impact, damage-feedback, mission-announcement, and input reset hooks. Restore authoritative values from the checkpoint while clearing or restore-epoch-scoping volatile damage deduplication, last-damage state, weapon input edges/receipts, shot and impact presentation histories, live effects, held/queued actions, and stale HUD feedback. Retain monotonic identifiers or epoch qualification so clearing transient caches cannot permit duplicate authoritative commits. Ensure every early failure unwinds to a quiescent, diagnosable state. Expose a compact restore receipt through existing runtime state for deterministic three-cycle verification. Do not optimize against the llvmpipe measurement; hardware performance recapture belongs in validation.
tasks.title: Make checkpoint restoration atomic and performance-verifiable
